subject: Model candidates, perf snapshots, and quality guardrails (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Cho <sam.cho@moderntools.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Model candidates, perf snapshots, and quality guardrails (post-call recap)

Hi Sam — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap + recommended next steps from our qualification call and the small eval plan we discussed.

Recap
- Primary goal: replace rule-based summarization pipeline in Modern Tools' support product with an LLM-driven summarizer that preserves privacy and stays within 150ms P99 budget on peak queries (target concurrent TPS ~60 for production pilot).
- Key constraints: strict data retention (30 days), on-prem option potential, cost target <$0.002/token effective.

Recommended candidate models (shortlist + verified perf)
1) Redwood-Opt-7B (ft-summary): best quality/cost balance for multi-turn summarization
   - Verified (Redwood perf profile): baseline throughput 85 TPS (seq len 512), p50 latency 18 ms/token, p95 72 ms/token on g4dn-equivalent
   - Notes: quantized q4f16 available for ~1.4x throughput improvement; expect small quality delta on long-context edge cases
2) LlamaX-13B-q4: better long-context coherence; throughput ~45 TPS (512), p95 ~95 ms/token
3) ClaudeLite-2.7B (fast variant): if ultra-low cost/latency tradeoff needed — 160 TPS baseline, but lower factuality on edge cases

Links: Redwood-verified perf profiles and bench artifacts
- Perf dashboard (Redwood): https://app.redwood.com/perf/ModernTools/DL-2026-0087
- Full benchmark bundle (traces, token-level p99): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-benchlinks/modern-tools-eval
- Prompt set & eval harness (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-promptsets/modern-tools-prompts

Quality & regression guardrails
- Suggested regression checks: ROUGE/ROUGE-L + semantic similarity (BERTScore) on a 200-example prompt set; monitor daily during pilot.
- Automatic fallback: route to fast ClaudeLite variant if p95 > 200ms for 2 consecutive 1-minute windows.
- Canary plan: small % of traffic (2%) -> 10% -> 50% over 48–72 hours. Rollback on quality drop >3% BERTScore or latency >SLA.

Next steps (ask)
- Confirm pilot scope (concurrent TPS target and retention constraints) — I've attached a draft pilot scope.
- Share a Slack/email for infra contact if you want us to include Private/VPC options in the cost estimate.
- Proposed pilot kickoff window: two-week runway starting 2026-09-27.

Attachments: pilot-scope-draft.pdf (outline of test traffic, metrics, and success criteria)

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Attachments: pilot-scope-draft.pdf

From: Sam Cho <sam.cho@moderntools.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model candidates, perf snapshots, and quality guardrails (post-call recap)

Thanks Tessa — helpful summary.
A few questions:
- The TPS numbers you quoted: are those for single server configs or for the Dedicated pool? We need p95 latency for 2048-token requests (most errors happen at ~2k tokens).
- For the regression alerting, can Redwood push webhook alerts into our PagerDuty? Also want daily digest to our analytics channel.
- Budget: if we start a 4-week pilot at avg 60 TPS with expected token sizes ~450, any high-level estimate?

I'll loop in our infra lead (cc'd here) if you want them involved. Also please share the prompt-set file so our SRE can run a smoke test.

Sam
Sam Cho
Head of Product, Modern Tools
sam.cho@moderntools.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Cho <sam.cho@moderntools.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Model candidates, perf snapshots, and quality guardrails (post-call recap)

Sam — answers inline.

- TPS numbers: perf profiles are measured on single GPU instances; Dedicated reserved pools can be scaled horizontally. The numbers I quoted are per-device baselines (seq len 512). For 2048 tokens, expect ~2.8x the per-token latency; I'll attach a quick cost/latency table in the Drive link. See perf dashboard for 2048 token traces.
- Webhooks/PagerDuty: yes — Redwood can emit alerts to your PagerDuty service and also post daily digests to a webhook/nginx endpoint. I'll have Vivek run the onboarding steps; we'll need an integration key.
- Pilot estimate: ballpark compute + tokens ~ $9k–$14k over 4 weeks for the Redwood-Opt-7B profile at 60TPS (avg token 450) — I'll convert to a detailed estimate and put it in the HubSpot deal.

Action items I've assigned:
- Vivek: prepare a pilot runbook + PagerDuty webhook integration checklist (attach prompt-set and onboarding steps). Deadline: 2026-09-16.
- Aditya: draft the cost estimate in HubSpot and share the link here.

cc: Vivek / Aditya — please confirm timelines.

Onboarding artifacts I'm attaching to this thread: prompt-set-v1.jsonl (small smoke corpus) — attached and also in Drive (link above).

Tessa
